## Proof

We find all $C^\infty$ solutions of
$$U_x=U_{yz},\qquad U_y=U_{zx},\qquad U_z=U_{xy}.$$

**Step 1. Three necessary conditions.**

Differentiate $U_x=U_{yz}$ w.r.t. $y$: $U_{xy}=U_{yyz}$. Since $U_z=U_{xy}$, this gives $U_z=U_{yyz}$, i.e.
$$(D_y^2-1)U_z=0. \tag{I}$$
Cyclically,
$$(D_z^2-1)U_x=0,\qquad (D_x^2-1)U_y=0. \tag{II,III}$$

**Step 2. Form of $U_x$ and $U_y$.**

From (II), treating $x,y$ as parameters, $U_x$ solves $F_{zz}=F$ in $z$, so
$$U_x=a(x,y)e^{z}+b(x,y)e^{-z}.$$
From (III), similarly,
$$U_y=c(y,z)e^{x}+d(y,z)e^{-x}.$$

**Step 3. Use $U_x=U_{yz}$.**

Since $U_{yz}=\partial_z U_y=c_z(y,z)e^x+d_z(y,z)e^{-x}$,
$$a(x,y)e^{z}+b(x,y)e^{-z}=c_z(y,z)e^{x}+d_z(y,z)e^{-x}\quad\forall x,y,z.$$
The right side lies in $\operatorname{span}\{e^x,e^{-x}\}$ as a function of $x$; varying $z$ and using the independence of $e^z,e^{-z}$ forces $a,b$ to lie in this span as functions of $x$:
$$a(x,y)=\alpha(y)e^x+\beta(y)e^{-x},\quad b(x,y)=\gamma(y)e^x+\delta(y)e^{-x}.$$
Thus
$$U_x=\alpha(y)e^{x+z}+\beta(y)e^{-x+z}+\gamma(y)e^{x-z}+\delta(y)e^{-x-z}.$$
Integrating in $x$,
$$U=\alpha(y)e^{x+z}-\beta(y)e^{-x+z}+\gamma(y)e^{x-z}-\delta(y)e^{-x-z}+F(y,z). \tag{$\ast$}$$

**Step 4. Use $U_y=U_{zx}$.**

From ($\ast$):
$$U_y=\alpha'(y)e^{x+z}-\beta'(y)e^{-x+z}+\gamma'(y)e^{x-z}-\delta'(y)e^{-x-z}+F_y(y,z),$$
$$U_{zx}=\alpha(y)e^{x+z}+\beta(y)e^{-x+z}-\gamma(y)e^{x-z}-\delta(y)e^{-x-z}.$$
Equating coefficients of the four independent exponentials $e^{x+z},e^{-x+z},e^{x-z},e^{-x-z}$:
$$\alpha'=\alpha,\quad -\beta'=\beta\ (\Rightarrow\beta'=-\beta),\quad \gamma'=-\gamma,\quad -\delta'=-\delta\ (\Rightarrow\delta'=\delta),\quad F_y=0.$$
Hence $\alpha=\alpha_0 e^y,\ \beta=\beta_0 e^{-y},\ \gamma=\gamma_0 e^{-y},\ \delta=\delta_0 e^y$, and $F(y,z)=G(z)$. Substituting into ($\ast$):
$$U=\alpha_0 e^{x+y+z}-\beta_0 e^{-x-y+z}+\gamma_0 e^{x-y-z}-\delta_0 e^{-x+y-z}+G(z). \tag{$\ast\ast$}$$

**Step 5. Use $U_z=U_{xy}$.**

From ($\ast\ast$):
$$U_z=\alpha_0 e^{x+y+z}-\beta_0 e^{-x-y+z}-\gamma_0 e^{x-y-z}+\delta_0 e^{-x+y-z}+G'(z),$$
$$U_{xy}=\alpha_0 e^{x+y+z}-\beta_0 e^{-x-y+z}-\gamma_0 e^{x-y-z}+\delta_0 e^{-x+y-z}.$$
All exponential terms match identically; the only remaining condition is $G'(z)=0$, so $G(z)=C_0$ (constant).

**Step 6. Conclusion and converse.**

Every solution therefore has the form
$$\boxed{\,U=A+B\,e^{x+y+z}+C\,e^{x-y-z}+D\,e^{-x+y-z}+E\,e^{-x-y+z}\,}$$
for arbitrary constants $A,B,C,D,E$.

Conversely, each term satisfies the system: for $e^{x+y+z}$ all first derivatives and the corresponding mixed derivatives equal $e^{x+y+z}$; for $e^{x-y-z}$, $U_x=e^{x-y-z}=U_{yz}$ (since $(-1)(-1)=1$), $U_y=-e^{x-y-z}=U_{zx}$ (since $(-1)(1)=-1$), $U_z=-e^{x-y-z}=U_{xy}$ (since $(1)(-1)=-1$); the two remaining exponentials $e^{-x+y-z}$ and $e^{-x-y+z}$ are checked identically (the signs of the first derivatives match the products of the signs in the mixed derivatives), and the constant term gives $0=0$. Hence every function of the displayed form is a solution.

## Proof

We find all $C^\infty$ solutions of
$$U_x=U_{yz},\qquad U_y=U_{zx},\qquad U_z=U_{xy}.$$

**Step 1. Three necessary conditions.**

Differentiate $U_x=U_{yz}$ w.r.t. $y$: $U_{xy}=U_{yyz}$. Since $U_z=U_{xy}$, this gives $U_z=U_{yyz}$, i.e.
$$(D_y^2-1)U_z=0. \tag{I}$$
Cyclically,
$$(D_z^2-1)U_x=0,\qquad (D_x^2-1)U_y=0. \tag{II,III}$$

**Step 2. Form of $U_x$ and $U_y$.**

From (II), treating $x,y$ as parameters, $U_x$ solves $F_{zz}=F$ in $z$, so
$$U_x=a(x,y)e^{z}+b(x,y)e^{-z}.$$
From (III), similarly,
$$U_y=c(y,z)e^{x}+d(y,z)e^{-x}.$$

**Step 3. Use $U_x=U_{yz}$.**

Since $U_{yz}=\partial_z U_y=c_z(y,z)e^x+d_z(y,z)e^{-x}$,
$$a(x,y)e^{z}+b(x,y)e^{-z}=c_z(y,z)e^{x}+d_z(y,z)e^{-x}\quad\forall x,y,z.$$
The right side lies in $\operatorname{span}\{e^x,e^{-x}\}$ as a function of $x$; varying $z$ and using the independence of $e^z,e^{-z}$ forces $a,b$ to lie in this span as functions of $x$:
$$a(x,y)=\alpha(y)e^x+\beta(y)e^{-x},\quad b(x,y)=\gamma(y)e^x+\delta(y)e^{-x}.$$
Thus
$$U_x=\alpha(y)e^{x+z}+\beta(y)e^{-x+z}+\gamma(y)e^{x-z}+\delta(y)e^{-x-z}.$$
Integrating in $x$,
$$U=\alpha(y)e^{x+z}-\beta(y)e^{-x+z}+\gamma(y)e^{x-z}-\delta(y)e^{-x-z}+F(y,z). \tag{$\ast$}$$

From ($\ast$):
$$U_y=\alpha'(y)e^{x+z}-\beta'(y)e^{-x+z}+\gamma'(y)e^{x-z}-\delta'(y)e^{-x-z}+F_y(y,z),$$

$$\alpha'=\alpha,\quad -\beta'=\beta\ (\Rightarrow\beta'=-\beta),\quad \gamma'=-\gamma,\quad -\delta'=-\delta\ (\Rightarrow\delta'=\delta),\quad F_y=0.$$

$$U=\alpha_0 e^{x+y+z}-\beta_0 e^{-x-y+z}+\gamma_0 e^{x-y-z}-\delta_0 e^{-x+y-z}+G(z). \tag{$\ast\ast$}$$
